# BgClear

> BgClear is a free, private, browser-based AI background remover. It removes image backgrounds entirely on the user's device — no signup, no watermark, no image upload to any server — and exports transparent PNG, JPG or WebP. It processes up to 20 images in one batch.

BgClear is an ad-supported web tool (not a paid product, no subscription). Background removal runs client-side in the browser using an open AI segmentation model, so photos never leave the device. First use of standard mode downloads a one-time ~30 MB model into the browser cache; an optional "High Quality Mode" (BiRefNet, ~490 MB, opt-in) targets difficult subjects such as logos, text and graphics. BgClear is a manual browser tool: it is **not** a hosted API and there is no downloadable server package.

Key facts:
- Free, ad-supported. No account, no credit card, no watermark.
- Processing is client-side. Images are not uploaded to a BgClear server.
- Batch limit: up to 20 images per run, processed sequentially.
- Input: JPG, PNG, WebP. Output: PNG (keeps transparency), JPG (no transparency), or WebP.
- Background options after removal: Transparent, White, Black, or a custom colour.
- Languages: English (default), Hindi, Italian, French, German, Turkish.
- Known weakness: built for subject isolation (people, products, pets, food); less reliable on logos, thin text, fine strokes and faint scanned signatures.

## Core tool

- [BgClear — Free Background Remover](https://bg-remover-free.netlify.app/): The main browser tool. Upload up to 20 images, remove backgrounds, choose Transparent/White/Black/custom, and download as PNG, JPG or WebP.
- [How AI background removal works](https://bg-remover-free.netlify.app/how-ai-works): Plain-English explanation of segmentation, edge detection and alpha matting.

Note: BgClear produces a visual image file. It does not certify that a photo will be accepted by any government authority or marketplace — always check the current requirements of the receiving body.

## Technical notes

- Background removal runs client-side; the AI model is fetched from a CDN at first use and cached by the browser. Repeat visits reuse the cached model.
- First use of standard mode downloads roughly 30 MB. High Quality Mode downloads roughly 490 MB and works best in a Chromium browser with WebGPU.
- Large images consume more memory; processing may fail on low-memory mobile devices.
- No backend image-processing service exists for this site.
